metaDescription: Six propane portable griddles from 17 to 24 inches compared by carry format, plate thickness, lid and zones for tailgates, campsites and small decks.
expertTake: The Blackstone OTG 22 inch with hard cover and two heat zones is the best portable griddle because it combines a proven plate with a lockable lid that makes travel simple. The Royal Gourmet PD1502H is the value pick for a compact two burner unit. Skip portable griddles if you want to cook indoors or on a balcony, because every model here burns propane. Test the setup once at home before you rely on it at a campsite.
introParagraphs: A portable griddle earns its place by how easily it travels and sets up, not by how big its plate is. The best ones pack down to a suitcase shape, survive a bumpy ride and are cooking within minutes of reaching the site. Put differently, a portable griddle is judged on the third trip, not the first.

Weight, lid design and how the legs work matter as much as the cooking surface. A griddle that is awkward to load or wobbles on uneven ground ends up staying home, however good the plate is. Test the setup at home first so the first cook at camp is not also the first assembly.

products.name: Blackstone OTG 22 Inch Tabletop Griddle with Hard Cover, 2 Zones
products.description:
The OTG with hard cover is a 22 inch tabletop griddle built for moving. The Omnivore plate arrives pre-seasoned and the hard cover closes over it like a clamshell, which protects the surface in a trunk and keeps wind off the burners at camp.

Two independently controlled heat zones give you a hot side and a cool side, which is enough for eggs on one side and sausage on the other. That is a better layout for travel than a single dial that makes the whole plate one temperature.

Compared with the OTG hooded 2350, this listing emphasises the hard cover and dual zones. It is a simple tabletop, so you need a sturdy table, and a cover and oil are still part of ownership. If you want one portable griddle without thinking too hard, this is the one. Setup is quick, since there is no stand to assemble, but make sure the table you use is level because a tilted plate pools oil to one side. Before the first trip, do a practice light in the driveway so you know how the ignition behaves. Bring a soft cover for storage as well, because the hard cover is for use and travel, not for long wet storage.
products.bestFor: Campers and tailgaters who want a lockable lid and two zones.
pros: Hard cover protects the plate in transit
Two independent zones for hot and cool sides
cons: Bare steel still needs oiling after every cook

products.name: Blackstone 2350 OTG 22 Inch Griddle with Hood, Flexfold Legs
products.description:
The 2350 differs from the other tabletop options by giving you folding legs and wheels. You can set it up at counter height without a table, then fold it and roll it away, which suits a driveway or a parking lot tailgate.

The locking hood is the detail that makes it travel well. It keeps the plate closed, clean and protected inside a vehicle.

The cost of legs and wheels is weight and complexity. Folding legs are a wear item, so check the latches after a season of use and keep the pivots clean. Against the hard cover OTG, you trade a simpler tabletop for the convenience of a built-in stand. Pick it if you do not want to carry a table, and skip it if you already have one. The folding mechanism is worth a deliberate test at home, because learning the latch sequence in a dark campsite is no fun. Wheels roll well on pavement and badly on soft grass or gravel. Park it level before you light it so oil does not pool.
products.bestFor: Tailgaters who do not want to carry a separate table.
pros: Folding legs give a built-in stand
Wheels make it easy to move
cons: Folding legs are a wear item

products.name: Royal Gourmet PD1502H 2-Burner Portable Griddle with Hood, 211 sq in
products.description:
The PD1502H is a compact two burner griddle with a plate listed at 3.5 mm thick and 211 square inches. The total output is 17,000 BTU across two independently controlled burners.

The 3.5 mm plate is below the 4 mm to 6 mm range that research favours for even heat, so expect it to be livelier and to show hot spots more readily than a heavy plate. At this size and price, that is an acceptable tradeoff for portability.

The hood keeps the plate clean in transit. With 211 square inches it handles a couple's breakfast or a small family's dinner, but it is the smallest cooking area among the 22 inch class in this guide. It is a sensible entry point for someone who wants to try griddle cooking without a large outlay. Keep expectations sensible at this plate thickness: preheat patiently, avoid dropping a tray of frozen food onto a blazing plate and let it recover between batches. Treated that way, it will do honest work for a long time. It pairs well with a small folding table.
products.bestFor: Couples and small families who want a low-cost entry to griddling.
pros: Hood included in the compact package
211 square inches in a small footprint
Light enough to carry by hand
cons: 3.5 mm plate is thinner than ideal
Smallest cooking area in the group

products.name: Royal Gourmet PD1301R 3-Burner Tabletop Propane Griddle, 24 Inch
products.description:
The PD1301R is the widest tabletop in this guide at 24 inches, with three separately controlled burners and 25,500 BTU in total. It is a tabletop design with sturdy feet for stability.

Three burners at this width let you run a hot end, a medium centre and a warm end, which is rare among portable griddles. The listing mentions a cover, which helps in transit.

It is bigger and heavier than the two burner models, so it is better for a car camping trip than a hike-in. Against the PD1502H, it offers more zone control and a wider plate at a higher tier. If you want the most capable tabletop in the group, this is it, provided you have a table that can take the weight. Plan your load for it, because a 24 inch tabletop with three burners is a two handed carry and wants its own space in the trunk. Check the burner knobs and feet for tightness after transport. Pack a flat scraper and a spare lighter.
products.bestFor: Car campers who want three zones on a tabletop.
pros: Three independent burners on a tabletop
24 inch width gives room for a family
cons: Larger and heavier than two burner units

products.name: VEVOR 2-Burner 22 Inch Portable Gas Griddle with Lid
products.description:
VEVOR's portable griddle lists a 22.24 by 16.3 inch cooking surface, which works out to about 362 square inches, more than the PD1502H's 211. It has two burners, a lid, an oil drain hole and an oil cup.

The drain and cup are the standout. Fat draining off the plate into a cup keeps the surface manageable and avoids pooling at camp, where you do not want a grease mess.

As a lesser known brand, VEVOR has less track record than Blackstone, so check parts and support. The lid is useful for transit and for protecting the plate. Against the Blackstone OTG units it offers a larger measured area for the money, with a less established design. Empty the cup before you pack, since oil sloshing around a trunk is the kind of surprise you only get once. Keep the lid latched while the plate is cooling so debris does not land on warm oil. Wipe the lid underside after cooking.
products.bestFor: Campers who want a bigger measured plate and an oil cup.
pros: About 362 square inches of cooking surface
cons: Less proven brand and parts supply

products.name: Blackstone 1814 17 Inch Portable Propane Griddle
products.description:
The 1814 is the smallest griddle in the group, a 17 inch stainless flat top. It is a solo or couple's griddle that fits in a cramped trunk or on a camp table with little room.

Seventeen inches cooks breakfast for two or a quick lunch, but it is not a family machine. Its stainless body resists weather better than a powder coated shell.

There is no hood or hard cover in the listing, so protect the plate with a cover and oil it after cooking. Compared with the OTG 22 inch models, it gives up area and the lid for the smallest packed size. It is the right pick for backpackers who drive and for small balconies where propane is allowed. It also suits owners who already have a bigger griddle at home and want a cheap, light companion for trips, rather than a main unit. Keep a small tin of oil with it.
products.bestFor: Solo travellers and couples with very little space.
pros: Smallest and lightest griddle in the group
cons: Small plate cannot feed a family

buyingCriteria.explanation: Tabletop units like the OTG hard cover and the PD1301R need a table, while the 2350 brings its own legs and wheels. A format mismatch is the main reason portable griddles stay home. Think about the last three places you would cook before you choose. It is worth imagining the full loading and unloading sequence, since a griddle you dread lifting will rarely leave the garage.

A lid protects the plate in transit and between cooks and helps with wind. The OTG hard cover, the 2350 hood, the PD1502H hood and the VEVOR lid cover this. The 1814 lacks one in the listing. Lids also keep insects and campfire ash off the plate, which is a bigger issue outdoors than at home.

Research favours 4 mm to 6 mm for even heat, and the PD1502H lists 3.5 mm. Thinner plates heat fast but show hot spots and can warp. Few portable listings state thickness. If the listing does not mention thickness, assume a thinner plate and cook accordingly with smaller batches.

VEVOR lists 22.24 by 16.3 inches, about 362 square inches, while the PD1502H lists 211 and the 1814 only 17 inches wide. A larger area helps when feeding more than two. A bigger plate is only a benefit if your propane supply and your table can handle it.

Two independent burners give a hot and a cool side, three give more nuance. The PD1301R has three, the OTG two, the 1814 fewer. Zones matter more than BTU. Two good zones beat three poor ones, so look at how separate the burners really are.
A drain and cup, as on the VEVOR, keeps camp tidy. Poor drainage turns a pleasant cook into cleanup. Check the cup size. Oil cups should be easy to remove with one hand while the plate is still warm.

specDecoder.meaning: Total burner output. Useful for fuel use, not for cooking quality. It rarely tells you how the machine feels at the table.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PD1301R lists 25,500 BTU, the PD1502H 17,000 BTU.

specDecoder.meaning: Metal depth between flame and food. It affects heat spread and warp resistance. Thin plates reward patience.
Independently controlled burners. They allow different temperatures at once. A zone is only useful if the flame can be turned down.
specDecoder.watchFor: The OTG lists two zones, the PD1301R three burners.

specDecoder.meaning: A built-in folding stand that removes the need for a table. Stand height should match your table and your back.
Actual plate dimensions in inches. It is more honest than the headline width. Always convert listings to square inches before comparing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Carry and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked folding legs, lids, wheels and tabletop formats. Units that set up quickly scored higher. The 2350 and the OTG hard cover led. We favoured fewer steps.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plate and area
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated plate thickness and measured area. The VEVOR's roughly 362 square inches led on area, while the PD1502H's 3.5 mm plate was the thinnest listed. Hot spots on thin plates were noted, not penalised heavily at this size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weather protection
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited lids, hoods and stainless bodies. Hard covers and hoods help in wind and rain. Units without one lost points. Stainless bodies earned small credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Zone control
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted separate burner controls. The PD1301R's three burners and the OTG's two zones scored well. Single burner layouts would have scored lower. Zone count mattered more than BTU.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read listings for repeat themes such as wobbly legs and thin plates. Those informed the cons and the order, not any numeric score. Cons reflect repeat themes only.

cards.label: Tabletop
cards.text: The OTG hard cover, PD1502H, PD1301R and 1814 need a table. They are lighter and simpler.

cards.label: Standing
cards.text: The 2350 brings folding legs and wheels. It is heavier but needs no table.

howToChoose.note: If your destination has a picnic table, choose tabletop. If it does not, choose the 2350. Either way, check the table can carry the weight and tolerate heat.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A lid that closes, a plate with wind guards and burners that are shielded. Wind steals heat and wastes fuel.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The OTG hard cover and the 2350 locking hood close fully. The Omnivore plates add wind guards.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You camp often and want the OTG's pre-seasoned plate or the 2350's legs and wheels.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use it a few times a year. The PD1502H or VEVOR gives you the cooking without the extras.

maintenance.why: Warm residue lifts easily. Waiting makes it stick. A dish scraper at a shallow angle works well.
A thin film keeps moisture away from steel. Travel humidity makes this more important. Use a high smoke point oil and wipe it nearly dry.
A full cup spills in the car. Empty it before packing. Pack the cup separately if it detaches.
Folding hardware loosens with repeated setup. Tighten before trips. A drop of light oil on the pivots helps.
Soapy water shows leaks as bubbles. Replace leaking parts. Do this with the cylinder disconnected from the ignition.

faq.a: A tabletop or folding format, a lid or hood and a weight you can carry. The 1814 is the lightest in this guide and the 2350 the easiest to move. Weight and format matter as much as plate size.
For tabletop units, yes, and it must tolerate heat underneath. The 2350 brings its own legs. A heat-safe mat under the legs adds a margin.

faq.q: How thick should the plate be?
faq.a: Research favours 4 mm to 6 mm for even heat. The PD1502H lists 3.5 mm, thinner than ideal. Thickness is a minor spec on a small plate but a major one on a large plate.

faq.q: Can I use one on a balcony?
faq.a: Propane is the most restricted fuel for balconies. Check fire code and your lease first. Rules follow the fuel, not the size of the unit.
Yes. Wind pulls heat off an open plate. A closed lid and wind guards reduce the loss. A hard cover or hood helps more than extra BTU.
Clean, oil and cover it, and keep it dry. Rust is the main enemy of a stored plate. Dry storage matters more than cover quality.
